daily_reality.summary: Radiologists interpret medical images (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, nuclear medicine) to diagnose conditions. They generate 10,000-14,000 wRVUs annually, reading 30-50+ studies per day. Work hours average 46/week. AI tools increasingly integrated into workflow.
typical_tasks: Interpret diagnostic imaging studies (CT, MRI, X-ray, ultrasound, mammography, PET)
Generate radiology reports with findings and recommendations
Consult with referring physicians on imaging findings
Perform image-guided procedures (biopsies, drainages) — interventional radiology
Participate in tumor boards and multidisciplinary case conferences
Monitor radiation dose and safety compliance
Manage worklist priorities and turnaround times
key_documents: Critical/urgent findings communication logs (RADPEER, ACR guidelines)
Informed consent for contrast and procedures
Quality assurance and radiation dose reports

deadlines.routine_reports: Same day or next day turnaround
deadlines.critical_findings: Immediate verbal communication to referring physician (ACR Practice Parameter)
deadlines.peer_review: Quarterly or annual depending on institution

daily_reality.seasonality: Imaging volume fluctuates slightly — higher during flu season and post-holiday periods. Summer slightly lower. On-call workload has grown 297% between 2006 and 2020.

regulatory.summary: Radiologists must have MD/DO, complete 5-year radiology residency, and obtain ABR board certification. State medical license required. FDA regulates imaging equipment. Radiation safety governed by NRC and state agencies. AI in radiology faces evolving FDA oversight.

key_laws.name: ABR Board Certification Requirements
key_laws.status: Active — effective July 2026: 4-year residency must be completed within 8 years

key_laws.name: NRC/State Radiation Safety Regulations
key_laws.status: Active — Agreement States regulate medical radiation use

requirements: MD or DO degree from accredited medical school
Optional 1-2 year fellowship (neuroradiology, MSK, body, breast, etc.)
ABR Qualifying (Core) Exam and Certifying Exam
DEA registration (if performing procedures with sedation)

regulatory.penalties: Practicing without license: felony. Failure to communicate critical findings: malpractice liability (radiology is #4 in malpractice claims). HIPAA violations: $100-$50K per incident. MQSA violations for mammography: facility sanctions.
controlling_bodies: FDA (imaging equipment and AI device clearance)
ACR (American College of Radiology — practice standards)

tools.summary: Radiologists work primarily through PACS (Picture Archiving and Communication System), RIS (Radiology Information System), and AI-assisted diagnostic tools. 2026 trend is unified RIS/PACS/AI platforms. Cloud-based solutions growing rapidly.

primary_tools.name: PACS (GE Centricity, Philips IntelliSpace, Sectra, Fujifilm Synapse)
primary_tools.description: Picture Archiving and Communication System — core platform for viewing and managing medical images

primary_tools.name: RIS (Radiology Information System)
primary_tools.description: Manages scheduling, workflow, reporting, and billing for radiology departments

primary_tools.name: Voice Recognition / Dictation (Nuance PowerScribe)
primary_tools.description: AI-powered speech recognition for radiology report generation

primary_tools.name: AI Diagnostic Tools (FDA-cleared algorithms)
primary_tools.description: Automated detection for findings like pulmonary embolism, fractures, intracranial hemorrhage — 500+ FDA-cleared AI devices for radiology

primary_tools.name: 3D Visualization and Advanced Post-Processing (TeraRecon, Vitrea)
primary_tools.description: 3D reconstruction, MPR, MIP for complex case review

secondary_tools: Clinical decision support (ACR Select, ACR Appropriateness Criteria)
Teaching file and case management systems
pain_points: Relentlessly increasing study volumes with flat staffing
Alert fatigue from AI tools generating excessive notifications
Poor integration between PACS, RIS, and EHR systems
Lack of standardization in AI algorithm validation and governance
Teleradiology creating 24/7 expectation for after-hours coverage

terminology.summary: Radiology uses extensive medical imaging terminology, standardized reporting lexicons (BI-RADS, LI-RADS, PI-RADS), and modality-specific jargon. ACR publishes practice parameters and appropriateness criteria.

terms.PACS: Picture Archiving and Communication System — digital image management
terms.RIS: Radiology Information System — workflow and scheduling management
terms.MRI: Magnetic Resonance Imaging — magnetic field-based imaging
terms.wRVU: Work Relative Value Unit — productivity measurement ($58/wRVU average)
terms.BI-RADS: Breast Imaging Reporting and Data System (ACR standardized reporting)
terms.LI-RADS: Liver Imaging Reporting and Data System
terms.PI-RADS: Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System
terms.contrast: Intravenous or oral agent to enhance imaging visibility
terms.enhancement: Increased signal/brightness in tissue after contrast administration
terms.stenosis: Narrowing of a vessel or passage
terms.edema: Swelling from fluid buildup visible on imaging
terms.DICOM: Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine — standard image format
terms.OLA: Online Longitudinal Assessment — ABR continuing certification requirement

career_psychology.summary: 13-year training path (undergrad + med school + residency + fellowship). Among highest-paid medical specialties ($470K-$580K). 54% burnout rate. AI augmenting rather than replacing radiologists. Severe workforce shortage projected through 2055.
career_path: Medical school — MD or DO (4 years)
Optional subspecialty fellowship (1-2 years: neuroradiology, body, breast, IR, etc.)
Section chief / Division director / Department chair
fears: AI replacing radiologists — persistent existential concern despite evidence against it
Missed critical findings on imaging — leading to malpractice
Commoditization through teleradiology driving down compensation
motivation: Lifestyle — fewer direct patient confrontations compared to surgical specialties
Critical role in patient diagnosis and treatment planning
burnout_factors: Relentless volume growth — on-call workload up 297% since 2006
Pressure for fast turnaround times (TAT metrics)

community.summary: Large and well-organized professional community. RSNA Annual Meeting is the world's largest radiology conference (~50,000 attendees). ACR sets practice standards. Multiple subspecialty societies.

associations.name: Radiological Society of North America (RSNA)
associations.type: World's largest radiology organization — research, education, annual meeting

associations.name: American College of Radiology (ACR)
associations.type: Professional organization — practice standards, appropriateness criteria, advocacy

associations.name: American Roentgen Ray Society (ARRS)
associations.type: Oldest radiology society in the US

events: RSNA Annual Meeting 2026 (Nov 29 - Dec 3, Chicago — McCormick Place)
online_communities: Radiopaedia — collaborative radiology resource and case library

market.summary: Structural radiologist shortage projected through 2055. Average salary $470K-$580K. 4% employment growth projected. AI augmenting not replacing — 500+ FDA-cleared radiology AI devices. 130 days average to fill a radiology position.

job_outlook.shortage: Significant projected through 2055 — exacerbated by post-COVID attrition
job_outlook.time_to_fill: 130 days average to fill a full-time radiology position
job_outlook.demand_drivers: Aging population, chronic disease, imaging utilization growth, rural access gaps

market_trends: AI integration as workflow augmentation — 500+ FDA-cleared devices
Unified RIS/PACS/AI platforms replacing siloed systems
Cloud-based PACS adoption growing rapidly ($3B+ market by 2032)
Teleradiology enabling remote reading but creating 24/7 demand
Subspecialization increasingly preferred over general diagnostic radiology
Only 10% of radiologists practice in rural areas serving 20% of population
